mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains elevated for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same period are not statistically lower than during the prior 60-day normalization window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive after controlling for lagged S&P 500 volatility (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected equity valuations and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in at least 60% of similar demand expansion episodes (backtest frequency).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 3% in a month suggests supply-side shocks that reduce future supply absorption, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 3% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite sustained INDPRO declines (Granger causality test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in the RSAFS exceeds +10% in a month, it indicates accelerated credit growth that may overheat the financial system, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by more than 10% in a single month
failure_condition: No significant negative 60-day forward returns are observed in analogous rapid credit growth periods (bootstrap p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining labor turnover (indicated by a downward trend in HOUST) suggest improved workforce stability, which reduces uncertainty and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST shows a continuous downward trend for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive after accounting for macroeconomic risk factors (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in consumer confidence proxies (e.g., a sharp one-month decline in UNRATE) coupled with rising industrial production (INDPRO) may create conflicting signals, but when UNRATE crosses below 4% while INDPRO remains flat for two months, it suggests a resilient labor market that drives positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% and remains below that level for two consecutive months while INDPRO remains within a 1% band
regime_hint: labor market resilience amid softening inflationary pressures
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in analogous regime windows (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In regimes where inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 3% for three consecutive months and short-term rates (FEDFUNDS) are steady, the S&P 500 tends to exhibit positive 20-day forward returns due to reduced policy uncertainty and improved risk sentiment.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 3.0 for three consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS change < 0.1% over the same period
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in at least 70% of similar low-inflation, steady-rate regimes (historical frequency).
